articles.headline: Vulnerabilities Found in Glamsterdam, Agents Came to the Rescue
articles.blurb: ChainSecurity flagged vulnerabilities in EIP-8037/8038, two state-pricing EIPs central to Glamsterdam's planned gas limit increase from 60M to 200M, with at least 13 major DeFi protocols identified as affected. The mechanism: EIP-8037's gas refill when storage slots are freed breaks the 1/64 gas guarantee in nested contract calls, enabling attackers to trigger outer-contract error handlers that lacked the gas to execute under the prior pricing model. Researchers from the Ethereum Foundation and Ethlabs each deployed AI agents overnight to scan for vulnerable contracts, then merged their efforts into a shared GitHub coordination repo where agents claim tasks via issue comments, deposit findings in structured directories, and produce consolidated memos without human intermediation. Core devs at the ACD paused any Glamsterdam launch date pending full impact analysis. The same agent-scanning framework is now running against EIP-8198 (Quick Slots, 12s to 10s slot time) ahead of Hegotá.

The growth mechanism is reflexive: options sellers hedge on perp markets, expanding perp OI rather than cannibalizing it, a dynamic Deribit already demonstrates with $2B+ in futures OI sourced from options hedging. September posted the best on-chain options month on record at ~$5B notional (7% of Deribit volume), with Derive commanding 90%+ of on-chain premium at $18B notional traded and DRV up 1,000%+ YTD at 66x annualized revenue.
